source_title: Celebrities ‘Someone You Love Will Leave...’: Anuradha Lekhi’s Post Hours Before Husband Sanjay Gupta's Death
source_excerpt:
Hours before filmmaker Sanjay Gupta tragically passed away at the age of 57 following an accidental fall at his Mumbai residence, his wife Anuradha Lekhi Gupta shared deeply poignant social media posts that have now left netizens in tears. The sudden demise of the acclaimed director, known for helming cult classics like Kaante , Shootout at Lokhandwala , and Shootout at Wadala, has left the Indian film industry in shock.
Following the news of his death, social media users noticed the heartbreaking timing of Anuradha’s Instagram posts, with one heartbreaking Reel on love and loss.
Roughly seven hours before the news of Gupta’s demise broke, Anuradha had shared an emotional reel on her Instagram handle depicting the journey of human life. In the video, a young girl excitedly asks about being born on Earth, prompting an older woman to explain what awaits her across the course of existence - from birth to death.
At one particularly moving juncture in the clip, the woman remarks, “The hardest part? Someone you love will leave before you do.” Following the filmmaker's sudden passing, the devastating dialogue has struck an intensely emotional chord with social media users, with many calling the timing surreal and gut-wrenching.

In addition to the reel, Anuradha had also posted a picture of a framed quote on her Instagram stories . It read, “ALWAYS BELIEVE THAT SOMETHING wonderful IS ABOUT TO HAPPEN.”
Accompanying the picture, she wrote a tender caption: “When you need some sort of reassurance...it will appear ” .

Sanjay Gupta and Anuradha Lekhi shared a resilient love story marked by deep companionship and second chances. After dating for nearly two and a half years, the duo tied the knot on 18 August 1997. However, the marriage hit a rough patch, eventually leading to a divorce in 2003.
Despite living apart for nearly six years, their bond remained unbroken. The filmmaker continually tried to win Anuradha back, and the couple eventually reconciled. In 2009, they remarried in an intimate ceremony held at a temple in Mumbai, starting fresh and building a family together. Sanjay Gupta is survived by Anuradha and their two children.
Sanjay Gupta was an acclaimed director known for helming cult classics like Kaante, Shootout at Lokhandwala, and Shootout at Wadala.
